title: DATA: Robotaxis in Phoenix have the lowest crash rate among major US cities
key_facts: IT Asset Management analysed federal data on self-driving vehicle collisions across the 5 metro areas with available data.
Phoenix had the lowest collision rate: 117 crashes, or 3.43 per million miles driven.
San Francisco was highest, followed by Atlanta, Austin and Los Angeles, each above 5 crashes per million miles.
Waymo is the only robotaxi operator in Phoenix; its service area covers 360 square miles.
Nationally, in one of every four crashes the robotaxi is rear-ended, and in more than half of reported collisions it was stopped or parked.
In one of every 10 crashes the robotaxi hit something stationary.
Phoenix injury crashes: 1.24 per million miles for human drivers against 0.47 for self-driving cars, 62 percent fewer.
quote_evidence: Phoenix recorded the lowest collision rate of any of them: 117 crashes, or 3.43 per million miles driven.
During the study period in Phoenix, human drivers were involved in 1.24 injury crashes per million miles.
Most of the time, the other driver hits the robotaxi.
why_it_matters_hint: A new analysis of federal crash reports finds Phoenix robotaxis crash least among five metros with data, and cause fewer injury crashes than human drivers there.
event_date: Study published about 2 Oct 2026; study period not stated
notes: Full article read. Study is by a company (IT Asset Management), reported by one local TV outlet; study dates and method are not given, and only 5 metros had data, so "major US cities" in the headline is broader than the data. Article opens with the outlet’s own framing that robotaxis "are safer than a human behind the wheel".
